title: Marine Bioacoustics
blurb: How can we detect, locate, and count whales with arrays of hydrophones? In the marine domain, I have worked on monitoring whales with wide-aperture arrays at sites in the Atlantic, Western Pacific, and Arctic oceans.

title: Terrestrial Bioacoustics
blurb: How can we improve passive monitoring of birds and other vocal animals through integrating principles across physical acoustics, array processing, and machine learning? On land, my work has focused on using compact microphone arrays to add a spatial dimension to bioacoustic monitoring, alongside explorations of learning useful representations of animal vocalizations.

title: Robotics
blurb: In late undergraduate and early graduate research, I worked on trajectory optimization and planning for systems including quadrotor drones, bipedal robots, and manipulator arms. While I am still very fond of optimization algorithms, there were no opportunities to contribute to wildlife conservation, and I pivoted my work to bioacoustics.
